data.title: Tandem’s Takeover of Compagnia dei Caraibi Clears 90% Threshold, Delisting Looms
data.description:
An announcement from Compagnia dei Caraibi S.p.A. ( (IT:TIME) ) is now available.

Tandem S.r.l.’s voluntary takeover bid for Compagnia dei Caraibi has closed with acceptances of 2,125,894 shares, equal to 56.507% of the shares subject to the offer and 14.683% of the issuer’s share capital. Together with shares acquired outside the offer and those already held by Gem S.r.l. and Trolley S.r.l., plus treasury stock, Tandem and concert parties are set to control 91.964% of the company.

This level of ownership exceeds the 90% threshold required to trigger squeeze-out procedures and pave the way for the delisting of Compagnia dei Caraibi from the market. As a result, there will be no reopening of the offer terms, and the purchase right and related purchase obligation will apply to the remaining 8.036% of the share capital, marking a shift toward full control by the offeror and reduced liquidity for minority shareholders.

data.title: HNO International Raises Capital via Dilutive Convertible Note
data.description:

On September 4, 2026, HNO International, Inc. entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement with CFI Capital LLC, issuing a convertible redeemable note with a principal amount of $210,000, including a $21,000 original issue discount for a net purchase price of $189,000. The note matures on September 4, 2027, carries 6% annual interest, and may be converted into common stock starting six months after issuance at a substantial discount to prevailing market prices, subject to a beneficial ownership cap and extensive share reservation commitments.

data.title: Tribal Group Agrees £189m Sale to Main Capital and Plans AIM Delisting
data.description:
Tribal Group plc ( (GB:TRB) ) has issued an update.

Tribal Group plc has agreed to sell all of its operating subsidiaries, including its Student Information Solutions division and Etio, to Thames Bidco Limited, a vehicle controlled by private equity investor Main Capital Partners, for approximately £189.3 million in cash. The deal, which constitutes a fundamental change of business under AIM rules and a restricted action under the Takeover Code, is subject to shareholder approval and satisfaction of a national security condition.

If the transaction completes, the board intends to delist Tribal’s shares from AIM and place the company into a members’ voluntary liquidation, distributing net sale proceeds to investors after covering PLC and liquidation costs from existing group cash resources. The board rejected an unsolicited, highly conditional alternative proposal from SilverTree Equity Partners, arguing Main Capital’s offer provides superior certainty and deliverability, while positioning Tribal to accelerate product innovation, cloud adoption and international expansion in a sector benefiting from strong structural growth trends.
